content: 1. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by influencing the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Clinical trials have shown that istradefylline at 40 mg/day increases the peak levels and area under the curve (AUC) of CYP3A4 substrates, while this effect is not observed at 20 mg/day. Dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates should be considered. 2. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of darunavir by influencing the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. At 40 mg/day, istradefylline increases the peak levels and AUC of CYP3A4 substrates, but this effect is not observed at 20 mg/day. Dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates should be considered. 3. Cobicistat and itraconazole mutually increase each other's levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. When itraconazole is coadministered with darunavir/ritonavir, the itraconazole dose should not exceed 200 mg/day. 4. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ivacaftor by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. The ivacaftor dose should be reduced when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Specific dosage adjustments should be made based on the ivacaftor-containing product. 5. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of ivacaftor by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. The ivacaftor dose should be reduced when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Specific dosage adjustments should be made based on the ivacaftor-containing product. 6. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of ixabepilone by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 7. Cobicistat and ketoconazole mutually increase each other's levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Specific dosage recommendations for ketoconazole are not available when coadministered with cobicistat. 8. Darunavir decreases the levels or effects of ketamine by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 9. Darunavir increases the levels of lacosamide by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Consider reducing the lacosamide dose when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 10. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of lansoprazole by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 11. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of lapatinib by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 12. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 13. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of darunavir by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Lenacapavir, as a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor, may increase the levels of CYP3A4 substrates initiated within nine months after the last subcutaneous dose, potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 14. Letermovir increases the levels of darunavir by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat increases the levels of letermovir by decreasing its metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Coadministration of letermovir, an OATP1B1/3 substrate, with OATP1B1/3 inhibitors may increase letermovir plasma concentrations. 15. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of levamlodipine by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Coadministration with moderate and strong CYP3A inhibitors increases systemic exposure to amlodipine and may require dose reduction. Monitor for symptoms of hypotension and edema to determine the need for dose adjustment. 16. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of levamlodipine by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Coadministration with moderate and strong CYP3A inhibitors increases systemic exposure to amlodipine and may require dose reduction. Monitor for symptoms of hypotension and edema to determine the need for dose adjustment. 17. Cobicistat and levoketoconazole mutually increase each other's levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Specific dosage recommendations for ketoconazole are not available when coadministered with cobicistat. 18. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of levomilnacipran by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Do not exceed 80 mg/day of levomilnacipran when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 19. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Coadministration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase plasma hormone concentrations. The use of a nonhormonal contraceptive is recommended. 20. Darunavir increases the levels of lidocaine by decreasing its metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 21. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of lidocaine by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Clinical monitoring is recommended upon coadministration with antiarrhythmics. 22. Darunavir decreases the effects of linagliptin by other mechanisms. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 23. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of linagliptin by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 24. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of losartan by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 25. Darunavir decreases the effects of liraglutide by other mechanisms. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors have been noted. 26. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of lofexidine by influencing CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Concomitant use with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors may increase lofexidine plasma levels. Monitor for symptoms of orthostasis and bradycardia, and consider dose reduction. 27. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of lopinavir by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 28. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of loratadine by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 29. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of losartan by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 30. Darunavir increases the levels of lumacaftor/ivacaftor by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Due to the induction effect of lumacaftor on CYP3A, the net exposure of ivacaftor at steady state is not expected to exceed that of ivacaftor monotherapy. No dose adjustment is necessary when CYP3A inhibitors are initiated in patients taking lumacaftor/ivacaftor. However, when initiating lumacaftor/ivacaftor in patients taking strong CYP3A inhibitors, reduce the dose to one tablet daily for the first week to allow for the steady-state induction effect of lumacaftor. Following this period, continue with the recommended daily dose. 31. Cobicistat increases the levels of lumacaftor/ivacaftor by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Due to the induction effect of lumacaftor on CYP3A, the net exposure of ivacaftor at steady state is not expected to exceed that of ivacaftor monotherapy. No dose adjustment is necessary when CYP3A inhibitors are initiated in patients taking lumacaftor/ivacaftor. However, when initiating lumacaftor/ivacaftor in patients taking strong CYP3A inhibitors, reduce the dose to one tablet daily for the first week to allow for the steady-state induction effect of lumacaftor. Following this period, continue with the recommended daily dose. No dose adjustment is required for moderate or weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. 32. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of lumateperone by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 33. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of lumateperone by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Reduce the dose to 5 mg/day if coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 34. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of lumefantrine by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 35. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of lumefantrine by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 36. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Maraviroc is a CYP3A4 substrate. Reduce the maraviroc dose to 150 mg BID when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 37. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Maraviroc is a CYP3A4 substrate. Reduce the maraviroc dose to 150 mg BID when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 38. Marijuana increases the levels or effects of darunavir by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 39. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of marijuana by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 40. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of mavorixafor by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored.
